answer: A stake-bonded reputation works like a glacier: slow to build, costly to fake. Each agent locks a deposit and earns trust only through verified work; a new identity starts with an onyx-black blank slate and no history, so spawning thousands of fakes buys nothing. A lantern of public attestations, peers vouching for real completed tasks, lights up genuine history, while an attacker must pay the bond and the time cost for every single fake, making a Sybil flood more expensive than any reward it could steal.
